author: Toll, Ian W.
title: Pacific Crucible: War at Sea in the Pacific, 1941–1942
publisher: W. W. Norton & Company, New York
notes: First of the Pacific War trilogy: Pearl Harbor to Midway, with a long opening on the Japanese naval establishment and its politics that is unusually good on why the war was begun. Toll is the readable modern narrative the arc will lean on for continuity, and he incorporates the post-1990s revisions — source:parshall-tully-2005 among them — that Morison predates. He is a synthesis, not an archive study: for a strength, a time or a position, prefer the official histories and cite Toll for the connective account. Unusually good on the Japanese side because it reads the post-war interrogations against the Japanese official history rather than through Fuchida. Verified against catalogue records only, not the volume in hand: ISBN 978-0-393-06813-9, LCCN 2011028907, OCLC 706023503, 597 pp. The 2012 date some catalogues give is the paperback — the Library of Congress call number is D767 .T65 2012 while the record's publication date is 2011, which is where the second date comes from (sand-lry.23).
